_about: Planner assumptions (guide section 7.3). Every value has a source; values marked 'derived' are our own arithmetic on a cited figure. All values are editable on the website. They are assumptions from published research and programme documents, not results from our own data. Compiled 27 Oct 2026; citations re-verified 27 Oct 2026.

howToRead.cost: One-off cost per household reached, in RWF (fuel not included). The improved cookstove uses the EAQIP subsidy (programme share); LPG and the electric pressure cooker use retail prices, so they are not on the same basis.
howToRead.usage: Share of households that actually use the new stove (sustained use). For the electric pressure cooker it is the share of cooking events, a weaker measure.
howToRead.effect: Share of a child's smoke-related risk of cough with fast breathing removed when the stove is used. Given as a range: 'trial' = randomised-trial point estimate; 'observational' = upper bound derived from observational studies.
howToRead.rankingNote: Cost, usage and effect are the same in every district, so they change the totals but not which districts come first.

effectEvidence.summary: Randomised trials, including HAPIN which had a site in Rwanda (Kayonza), did not show a statistically significant reduction in severe infant pneumonia from LPG cooking (IRR 0.96, 98.75% CI 0.64-1.44). Observational studies associate solid-fuel use with higher child pneumonia risk (pooled OR 1.78). Our own Rwanda survey model also finds no significant fuel effect after adjustment. Cases averted are therefore shown as a range of scenarios, not a prediction. Trial outcomes are severe or physician-diagnosed pneumonia in infants and young children; our outcome is mother-reported cough with fast breathing in children under 5, so these effects are borrowed from a different, more specific outcome, not measured in our data. The observational values are upper bounds: they assume the association is fully causal and the exposure fully removed.

sources.finding: LPG intervention: severe pneumonia in the first year of life (imaging- or oximetry-confirmed, or verbal autopsy) 5.67 vs 6.06 per 100 child-years, IRR 0.96 (98.75% CI 0.64-1.44); child PM2.5 median 24.2 vs 66.0 ug/m3
sources.citation: McCollum ED et al. (HAPIN Investigators). N Engl J Med 2024;390:32-43

sources.finding: Unprocessed solid fuel use and pneumonia/ALRI in children under 5: pooled odds ratio 1.78 (95% CI 1.45-2.18)
sources.citation: Dherani M et al. Bull World Health Organ 2008;86(5):390-398

sources.finding: Chimney woodstove, children <18 months: physician-diagnosed pneumonia RR 0.84 (95% CI 0.63-1.13); authors report a significant reduction of about a third in severe pneumonia (exact estimate not verified)

Advanced-combustion biomass stoves cut kitchen PM2.5 by 41% (29-50%); personal PM2.5 exposure fell 55% (19-87%) for solid-fuel stoves with chimneys (no personal estimate given for advanced combustion); levels stay above WHO guidelines
sources.citation: Pope D et al. Environment International 2017;101:7-18

stoves.name: LPG gas stove
stoves.costSource: Gas stove alone 'as much as' Rwf 150,000 ($120) per KT Press, 29 Oct 2025 (the programme kit of 2-burner stove + 12 kg cylinder + smart pay-as-you-go valve is described separately, with no kit price given): https://www.ktpress.rw/2025/10/50000-households-to-get-free-cooking-gas-kits-courtesy-of-rwanda-saudi-deal/ . Refill not included: Rwf 23,340 per 12 kg at SP stations (Rwf 1,945/kg) and Rwf 27,000-28,000 at retailers, New Times 22 Apr 2026 https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/35066/news/energy/why-gas-retailers-are-charging-different-prices-across-rwanda ; one 12 kg cylinder lasts up to ~2 months (KT Press).
stoves.usageSource: Assumption (not a measured value). HAPIN trial: biomass stove used on a median 0.4% of monitored days, but with free LPG and close monitoring. Real-world use is likely lower; no Rwanda field data found. Lower this value to test refill-cost risk.
stoves.effectSource: trial = 1 - IRR 0.96 (HAPIN, severe infant pneumonia, not significant); observational = 1 - 1/1.78 = 0.438 (derived from the Dherani 2008 pooled odds ratio; upper bound assuming causality and full exposure removal)

stoves.name: Improved biomass cookstove (Tier 3)
stoves.costSource: EAQIP clean-cooking results-based financing: worked example of a Tier 3 stove priced Rwf 45,000 with a Rwf 36,000 subsidy (household pays 9,000). Rule as of Ver 05 (1 Mar 2024): Tier 3 subsidy 80%, cap Rwf 38,000. BRD, EAQIP Component 3b Clean Cooking RBF Operations Manual Ver 05 (1 Mar 2024; the file name says Ver03), section 6.7 and Table 2: https://www.brd.rw/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/EAQIP_CC-RBF_OM_-_Ver_0306-04-2022.pdf . Use 45,000 for full price without subsidy.
stoves.usageSource: Rwanda, free EcoZoom stoves to 101,778 households: about a year after distribution, 83.3% (25 of 30) of households seen cooking were using it, and 89.3% reported it as their primary stove; 51.3% reported also using other stoves. Barstow CK et al. BMC Public Health 2016;16:584 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4947312 . Pilot reported exclusive use was only 28.5% over 5 months (Barstow et al. PLoS One 2014;9:e92403).
stoves.effectSource: trial = 1 - RR 0.84 (RESPIRE chimney stove, physician-diagnosed pneumonia, not significant); observational = 0.438 x 0.41 = 0.18 (derived: Dherani upper bound scaled by the 41% kitchen PM2.5 reduction for advanced-combustion stoves in Pope 2017; assumes risk falls in proportion to exposure, which likely overstates benefit)

stoves.name: Electric pressure cooker
stoves.costSource: List price Rwf 85,000 (pilot discounted to Rwf 40,000), electricity not included. SEforALL 2023, Examining the Experience of Using EPCs in Urban Households in Kigali: https://www.seforall.org/system/files/2023-11/report-rwanda-clean-cooking-final.pdf
stoves.usageSource: Kigali pilot (n=100 grid-connected charcoal/LPG households, ~2-3 months of EPC use, Mar-May 2023): EPC used in 41% of cooking events (not share of households); charcoal meals fell from 67% to 45%. SEforALL 2023, Examining the Experience of Using EPCs in Urban Households in Kigali: https://www.seforall.org/system/files/2023-11/report-rwanda-clean-cooking-final.pdf . Longer follow-up not found.
stoves.effectSource: Clean fuel, same evidence as LPG (no EPC-specific health trial found). Applies only to meals cooked on the EPC, which the usage rate captures.

programmeContext.fact: EAQIP clean-cooking target: 500,000 households (by 2026); US$17M for results-based subsidies + US$3M technical assistance
programmeContext.source: BRD EAQIP CC-RBF Operations Manual Ver 05 (2024), section 1

programmeContext.fact: National target reported for 2029: biomass cooking from 79.9% to 42% of households; clean cooking from 9% (2024) to 22%
programmeContext.source: AllAfrica / New Times, 2 Nov 2025 (does not name the NST2 document directly)

programmeContext.fact: Subsidy for pay-as-you-go/credit sales is paid 50% on verified sale, 40% after a 3-month use check, 10% after 1 year (cash sales: 80% / 20%)
programmeContext.source: BRD EAQIP CC-RBF Operations Manual Ver 05 (2024), Table 3

plannerDisclaimer: Stove effect, usage and cost are editable assumptions from published research and programme documents, not results from our data. Trials measured severe or doctor-diagnosed pneumonia in infants; we apply their effects to cough with fast breathing in children under 5, so 'cases averted' is an illustrative range, not a prediction.
